newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mayne says reviews Optus sale options.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mayne says reviews Optus sale options.

text.p: Transport, security and health care group Mayne Nickless said on Thursday its 25 percent owned Optus Communications had earnings before tax of A$59 million for the six months to December 31, up from A$7 million a year ago.
Mayne said also in a statement accompanying its half year results that it is considering four other options to achieve a sale of its shareholding in Optus.

"Mayne Nickless' preferred option for the sale of its 25 percent shareholding continues to be by way of a float of Optus Communications, but this will remain unlikely whilst litigation continues," Mayne said.
Mayne said it was considering four other options to achieve a sale, in addition to the float.
"We are not in a position to detail these options, but they are aimed at allowing a sale process by June/July 1997," managing director Bob Dalziel said in a statement.
"Mayne Nickless will continue to pursue these options in parallel and will continue to inform the market of developments," he said.
Mayne said Optus recorded revenue for the six months of A$1.195 billion, up 32 percent on the previous corresponding period.
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation were A$309 million, a 69 percent increase on the previous corresponding period.
"The operational performance of Optus Communications has been outstanding," Mayne said.
"The postponement of the float...because of legal action involving Optus Vision shareholders has been frustrating," it added.
Mayne has said it plans to sell its stake in order to focus on its core businesses.
Optus Communications had planned to float last year, but the process has been held up by a dispute between shareholder in its associate, Optus Vision, and the Seven Network.
